postings.conferenceName: Real-Time Conversational Agents Workshop at NeurIPS 2026
postings.conferenceText: Real-Time Conversational Agents (RTCA) Workshop @ NeurIPS 2026Sydney, Australia — 11 or 12 December 2026Website: https://rtcaneurips26.github.io/Submission portal (OpenReview): https://openreview.net/group?id=NeurIPS.cc/2026/Workshop/RTCA*** Submission deadline: 29 August 2026 (Anywhere on Earth) ***We are pleased to share the Call for Papers and Demos for the inaugural Real-Time Conversational Agents (RTCA) Workshop, held in conjunction with NeurIPS 2026 in Sydney, Australia.OVERVIEWConversational AI has moved from text chat into the real world — voice modes, embodied avatars, and agents that share our screens and tools. To feel natural, these systems must operate in real time: streaming speech, video, and language while continuously listening, watching, and re-planning. This is fundamentally harder than offline generation — latency, turn-taking, backchannels, interruptions, and cross-modal alignment all become first-class problems that the offline-generation paradigm largely sidesteps. Recent progress on full-duplex speech-language models, real-time talking-head and avatar generation, low-latency speech synthesis, and streaming ASR shows that interactive multimodal agents are now technically feasible, but the field still lacks shared benchmarks, vocabulary, and methodology for interactional naturalness as distinct from per-utterance quality.RTCA brings together researchers across speech, vision, language, HCI, social-signal processing, and ML systems around three intertwined questions:Real-time generation under hard latency budgets — producing high-quality speech, video, and language in a streaming or full-duplex fashion.Naturalness in interaction — what makes an agent feel like a conversational partner (prosody, gaze, timing, grounding, expressivity, turn-taking).Evaluation of live systems — measuring naturalness, responsiveness, and conversational quality where standard offline metrics fall short.TOPICS OF INTEREST (non-exhaustive)Streaming/low-latency speech synthesis, ASR, and full-duplex audio-language modelsReal-time talking-head, avatar, and embodied video generation; lip-sync, gaze, expressivity under streamingStreaming language models; incremental and speculative decoding for dialogueTurn-taking, backchanneling, interruption handling, and floor managementMultimodal alignment under latency and partial-observation constraintsProsody, emotion, and paralinguistic generation in interactive settingsMemory, grounding, and tool use during live conversationEvaluation of naturalness: perceptual studies, turn-taking metrics, perceived latency, interactive Turing-style testsDatasets and benchmarks for interactive (not offline) evaluationEfficient inference, on-device deployment, and the systems-quality trade-offSafety, identity, and trust in real-time agents (deepfakes, persuasion, consent)Position papers, critiques of current evaluation practice, and reproducibility studies are also welcome.SUBMISSION TYPESFull papers (up to 8 pages) — original contributions; may be presented as posters and/or contributed talks.Short papers (up to 4 pages) — work in progress, focused contributions, or position papers.Demo papers (extended abstract or up to 2 pages) — required for the on-stage Conversational Agents Showcase.All submissions must use the NeurIPS 2026 style file and be formatted for double-blind review. Page limits exclude references and appendices. Papers must be submitted in PDF format via OpenReview. The workshop is non-archival; authors retain the right to publish elsewhere.IMPORTANT DATES (End of day, Anywhere on Earth)Call for papers opens: 18 July 2026Submission deadline (papers and demos): 29 August 2026Author notification: 29 September 2026Workshop date: 11 or 12 December 2026CONFIRMED INVITED SPEAKERSDimitris Samaras — Stony Brook University, USAEvonne Ng — Meta Reality Labs / UC Berkeley, USAORGANISERSNiki Foteinopoulou — Tavus, United KingdomAlessandro Conti — Tavus, ItalyJack Saunders — Tavus, United KingdomOya Celiktutan — King's College London, United KingdomCigdem Beyan — University of Verona, ItalyIoannis Patras — Queen Mary University of London, United KingdomCONTACTFor more information, visit https://rtcaneurips26.github.io/ or contact us at rtca-workshop@googlegroups.com.We look forward to your contributions.

CMRMV welcomes 1) full papers presenting significant research, development, application, position, or survey, 2) short papers on work-in-progress, 3) posters, 4) contributed talk presentations, as well as workshops, thematic sessions, and demos.Prospective authors are invited to submit original, unpublished works, which are not under review in any other conference or journal.IMPORTANT DATES:Submission deadline: August 21, 2026Notification: September 15, 2026Registration: October 1, 2026Camera Ready: October 10, 2026Themes of interest include, but are not limited to:Advanced Control Systems and Agentic PerspectiveMechatronic Systems Design and IntegrationRobotics Systems and ArchitecturesMachine Vision and Perception SystemsIntelligent and Learning-Based SystemsAutonomous Systems and NavigationHuman - Robot Interaction and Collaborative SystemsAgentic Architectures for Autonomous Physical SystemsEmerging Applications and Future DirectionsFor more information on topics, submission types, satellite events, etc., please visit the conference website at https://www.dtrsociety.org/cmrmv2026/Conference ChairsLect. postings.conferenceName: 1st International Colloquium on Artificial Intelligence & Cybersecurity for Healthcare and Social Good
postings.conferenceText: Welcome to AISEC4HSG’2026The first edition of the International Colloquium on Artificial Intelligence & Cybersecurity for Healthcare and Social Good (AISEC4HSG’2026) will be held on September 25–26, 2026 at the City of Innovation (CIM), Cadi Ayyad University, Marrakech, Morocco. The colloquium will be organized in a hybrid format, enabling participants to attend either in person or remotely.AISEC4HSG’2026 brings together PhD students, academic researchers, and industry professionals from diverse backgrounds to present and exchange innovative ideas, recent advances, and cutting-edge research in Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, and Intelligent Systems and Technologies for Healthcare and Social Good.The colloquium provides a premier interdisciplinary platform for researchers, practitioners, educators, and policymakers to discuss the latest innovations, trends, challenges, and ethical implications, as well as practical solutions related to AI-driven and cybersecurity-enabled technologies. It also seeks to foster scientific collaboration, networking, and interdisciplinary partnerships among participants from academia, industry, and research institutions.AISEC4HSG’2026 further offers PhD students and early-career researchers the opportunity to strengthen their theoretical and practical knowledge, interact with leading specialists, and explore recent scientific breakthroughs in Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Intelligent Systems, and Advanced Computing Technologies.Participants will discover emerging technologies, innovative methodologies, and real-world applications in computing, networking, intelligent systems, and cybersecurity that are driving the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence applied to healthcare and social good. Special attention will be devoted to the ethical, societal, legal, economic, and security challenges raised by the AI and cybersecurity revolution, with the aim of promoting responsible, trustworthy, and human-centered innovation.Through this event, the colloquium aims to:Provide an interdisciplinary forum to discuss innovations, challenges, and ethical implications of AI-driven and cybersecurity-enabled technologies.Foster scientific collaboration and networking among academia, industry, and research institutions.Support PhD students and early-career researchers in strengthening their theoretical and practical expertise.Explore the societal, economic, and technological impact of Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity across a wide range of application domains.Promote responsible, trustworthy, and human-centered innovation.The discussions will explore the opportunities offered by these interconnected disciplines and their societal, economic, and technological impact, particularly in the following areas:Healthcare and well-beingEducation and learningIndustryTransportationEnvironmentAgricultureEnergyClimate changeSocial and personal developmentSocial innovationSmart citiesGovernance

postings.conferenceName: 2027 7th International Conference on Robotics and Control Engineering (RobCE 2027)
postings.conferenceText: Call for Papers2027 7th International Conference on Robotics and Control Engineering (RobCE 2027) Shenzhen, China | May 20-23, 20272027 7th International Conference on Robotics and Control Engineering (RobCE 2027) will take place in Shenzhen, China during May 20-23, 2027, which is organized by Southern University of Science and Technology and Southeast University, supported by The Hong Kong Polytechnic University - Nanjing Technology and Innovation Research Institute, Hong Kong Society of Mechanical Engineers (HKSME). Focusing on the international research and key application domains of robot and control engineering, around the theme of "AI-Driven Intelligent Control and Next-Generation Robotic Systems", RobCE 2027 is going to conduct high level academic communication and display the latest achievements, build the international collaborative innovation platform.We warmly welcome prospective authors to submit your research papers to RobCE 2027, and share your latest research results and valuable experiences with other top-scientists, engineers and scholars from all over the world.● Publication & IndexingAll the registered and presented papers will be included in the volume of ACM International Conference Proceedings Series (ICPS), the publisher will submit articles to Engineering Village, Scopus, Web of Science and other databases for review and indexing after publication.● Call for Papers – TopicsTopics of interest for submission include, but are not limited to:Track I: Robot Perception, Navigation and ControlTrack II: Embodied Intelligence and Robot LearningTrack III: Autonomous Robot SystemsTrack IV: Industrial Robot Control and ApplicationTrack V: Human-Robot Interaction ControlTrack VI: Robot Control Theory and MethodsTrack VII: Novel Robot Design and AnalysisTrack VIII: Rehabilitation and Medical Robot TechnologyTrack IX: AI-Driven Robot SystemsTrack X: Robot Industrialization and ApplicationTrack XI: Tele-robot and Its Applications● Submission MethodPlease submit your paper through submission system:https://cmt3.research.microsoft.com/RobCE2027If you have any question about submission: info_robce@vip.163.com●Submission Note1. The manuscript must be written in English;2. The manuscript should be written in accordance with the standard of template;3. The topics of manuscript should be relevant to conference topics;4. The manuscript should be no less than 8 pages (Single column) or 5 pages (Double columns);5. Plagiarism and duplicate submission are prohibited;6. Innovation and scientific value are essential.●ContactMs. Joy Mou ( Conference Secretary)E-mail: info_robce@vip.163.comTel: +852-30506862Website: https://robce.org/

As a well-established annual event, the International Conference on Education and Training Technologies (ICETT) has maintained its legacy of fostering knowledge exchange and collaboration in the realm of education and training technologies. Commencing with its inaugural edition held in China in 2014, ICETT has successfully organised editions in diverse locations such as Singapore, Finland, South Korea, and more.The city of Seoul, renowned for its dynamic blend of tradition and modernity, provides a perfect setting for ICETT 2027. With its vibrant cultural scene, world-class infrastructure, and rich history, Seoul offers an inspiring environment for knowledge sharing, collaboration, and networking among global scholars and An additional page fee will be charged for pages starting from the 6th page.Abstract (Oral Presentation only, without publication):Authors interested in presenting at a conference may choose to submit only an abstract (200-400 words). You'll give an oral presentation at the conference if your abstract is accepted, but your paper will NOT be published.Abstract Template: https://www.icett.org/Abstract%20Template.docNo Submission:If you only want to attend the conference without any submission, please just register as Delegates.Submission Method (PDF Only)Please choose one method only. postings.conferenceText: About the ConferenceThis is the conference of the SIAM Activity Group on Applied & Computational Discrete Algorithms. ACDA27 brings together researchers who design and study combinatorial and graph algorithms motivated by applications. ACDA27 is organized by SIAM under the auspices of its Activity Group on Applied and Computational Discrete Algorithms. ACDA27 includes in its scope all topics where models and algorithms from discrete mathematics are applied to solve problems in computer science, scientific computing, data science, physical sciences, life sciences, engineering, social and information sciences, etc. ACDA27 invites papers on the formulation of combinatorial problems from applications; theoretical analyses; design of algorithms; computational evaluation of the algorithms; and deployment of the resulting software to enable applications.The ACDA27 conference will include refereed proceedings as well as talks without proceedings papers (in the conventional SIAM style of conferences), posters, tutorials, invited talks, and industry sessions. Awards will be given for best paper, best poster, and best student presentation. Proceedings of the first three ACDA conferences organized in 2021, 2023, and 2025 are available here.  The following conference will be held jointly:SIAM Activity Group on Computational Science and Engineering (CSE27) The following workshop will be held jointly:SIAM International Meshing Roundtable Workshop 2027 (IMR27)Connect with other attendees on LinkedIn. Included ThemesTopics of interest include, but are not limited to, discrete or combinatorial problems and algorithms arising in:    Algorithm engineering    Algorithmic differentiation (AD)    Combinatorial optimization and mathematical programming, including scheduling and resource allocation problems    Combinatorial scientific computing (CSC), including models, algorithms, applications, numerical methods, and problems arising in data analysis    Computational biology and bioinformatics    Data management and data science    Design and analysis of application-inspired exact, approximation, randomized, streaming, and learning-augmented algorithms    Graph and hypergraph algorithms, including problems arising in network science and complex networks    Interaction between algorithms and modern computing platforms, including challenges arising from memory hierarchies, accelerators, and novel memory technologies    Machine learning and statistical methods for solving combinatorial problems    Numerical linear algebra, including sparse matrix computations and randomized approaches    Parallel and distributed computing, including algorithms, architectures, distributed systems, and all parallelism ranging from instruction-level and multi-core all the way to clouds and Exascale computing    Other applications arising from security, computational finance, computational chemistry/physics, quantum computing, etc.

postings.conferenceName: The Second WACE WebAssembly, Cloud and Edge: Shaping the Future of Computing (WACE) Workshop
postings.conferenceText: The Bytecode Alliance in partnership with Ghent University - imec and the ELASTIC project is pleased to organize and host the second WACE workshop: WebAssembly, Cloud and Edge: Shaping the Future of Computing (WACE).The workshop will be co-located with the ACM Middleware conference 2026, taking place 14th – 18th December 2026 in Tarragona, Spain.We invite submissions of papers and welcome presenters and participants to join us at this exciting event.[ Submission and Important Dates ]    Submission deadline: 17 September 2026    Acceptance Notification: 12 October 2026    Camera-ready deadline: 16 October 2026    Submission site: https://wace2026.hotcrp.com/[ Topics of Interest ]Lightweight and cross-platform software distribution, sandboxing and orchestration are important challenges for cloud-native and edge systems. The cloud-edge continuum paradigm specifically introduces additional requirements such as strong isolation guarantees between tenants, seamless migration across multiple CPU architectures, and cold start times in the order of milliseconds. An increasing threat landscape and complex software supply chains introduce the need for high-performance software sandboxing in a large breadth of use-cases ranging from in-application plugin frameworks to microcontrollers with Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS). Emerging technologies such as WebAssembly and MicroVMs are promising technologies to address these challenges.This workshop invites research aiming to address the challenges of software distribution and sandboxing across cloud, edge and IoT platforms. Topics include:*    Containerization, and virtualization technologies such as WebAssembly and MicroVMs*    Cross-platform application distribution on architectures such as RISC-V and ARM*    Hardware abstraction and access layers such as the WebAssembly System Interface (WASI)*    Workload orchestration and resource management across the Edge-Cloud Continuum.*    Application composability and universal plugin systems, including for microcontrollers and real-time operating systems.*    Software isolation and access control, including in multi-tenant systems[ Author Instructions ]We invite original research papers that have not been previously published and are not currently under review for publication elsewhere.*    Submitted workshop papers should be no longer than 6 pages in the standard ACM format.*    The review process is single blind*    Submit your article here: https://wace2026.hotcrp.com/*    Note that at least one author of each accepted workshop paper must hold a full pre-conference registration.*    For the camera-ready instructions, please visit the camera-ready instructions page: https://middleware-conf.github.io/2026/camera-ready-instructions/A “Best Paper Award” certificate will be conferred on the author(s) of a paper presented at the workshop, selected by the Chairs based on scientific significance, originality and outstanding technical quality of the paper, as assessed also by the evaluations of the members of the Program Committee.[ Workshop Description ]The workshop will be organised as a half-day event and will contain a mix of invited talks from industry experts and peer-reviewed scientific contributions. This format was chosen to increase interaction between industry and academia, and attract a diverse audience.The workshop programme will include:*    Scientific technical sessions with peer-reviewed workshop contributions that will be published as part of the conference proceedings.*    Invited talks from industry and ecosystem experts, focusing on real-world deployments, architectures, and lessons learned. These talks will not be included in the conference proceedings.

postings.conferenceName: International Colloquium on Automata, Languages and Programming
postings.conferenceText: ICALP is the flagship conference and annual meeting of the European Association for Theoretical Computer Science. It was launched in 1972 and covers the breadth of theoretical computer science.The scientific programme is traditionally organized around two main tracks: Algorithms, Complexity, and Games, and Automata, Logic, Semantics, and Theory of Programming. Typical topics include algorithms, automata theory, computational complexity, logic, semantics, verification, type systems, models of computation, and related areas.

postings.conferenceName: 17th Symposium on Software Performance
postings.conferenceText: The 17th Symposium on Software Performance (SSP) will take place in Würzburg, Germany, from 09 to 11 November 2026.The submission portal is now open (https://cmt3.research.microsoft.com/SSP2026).In addition to invited talks from practitioners and researchers, we welcome contributions from academic, scientific, and industrial contexts within the field of software performance. This includes, but is not limited to, approaches employing Descartes, Kieker, and/or Palladio.*Scope*Submissions are invited for plans, ongoing work, or results regarding:   *     Software quality analysis with regard to: performance; scalability and         elasticity; energy efficiency; dependability and resilience; security         and privacy   *     Application performance measurement and management   *     Performance measurement and benchmarking   *     Performance modelling (modelling concepts, simulation, extraction, and         calibration)   *     Automated run-time management of software systems   *     Automated approaches for performance problem detection, diagnosis, and         resolution   *     Performance-related challenges in industrial software systems   *     Application of Descartes, Kieker, or Palladio in projectsPlease note that we explicitly welcome contributions that have already been (partially) presented at other events or in prior publications.*Types of Contributions *We solicit the following types of contributions:   *     Technical papers (maximum 3 pages, including references)   *     Extended abstracts for industry or experience talks (max. 700 words)*Submission Guidelines *Technical papers should follow the Softwaretechnik-Trends format and must be submitted electronically via Microsoft CMT. Extended abstracts must be submitted as "abstract only" submissions (both in text and PDF format) via Microsoft CMT as well.We strongly encourage you to use our LaTeX template for your technical paper to minimize the need for adjustment if your submission is accepted. Make sure that the document uses a Times/Computer Modern font in 10 pt and that the paper size is A4.*Publication*At least one author of each accepted paper is required to register, attend the conference, and present the paper. Accepted papers will appear in the GI Softwaretechnik-Trends.*Submission Deadlines*   *     17 August 2026; 23:59 AoE: Abstract submission (for all paper types)   *     24 August 2026; 23:59 AoE: Paper submission   *     13 September 2026: Acceptance notification   *     14 to 27 September 2026: Shepherding phase   *     12 October 2026: Camera-ready paper submissionYou can find further details on the symposium website: https://www.performance-symposium.org

postings.conferenceText: 3rd International Conference on Digital Sovereignty (ICDS) 2026Publisher: Springer Proceedings in Complexity (Indexed in Scopus, DBLP, WoS, Level 1 in NSD)Welcome to ICDS 2026!It is with great pleasure to welcome you to the Third International Conference on Digital Sovereignty (ICDS 2026), which will be organised by the Institute for Energy Technology (IFE) from November 25th – 27th, 2026, in Oslo, Norway.The International Conference on Digital Sovereignty (ICDS) is the world’s only dedicated conference exclusively focused on digital sovereignty, addressing one of the most critical challenges shaping today’s digital future. Established in 2024, ICDS has rapidly emerged as a unique global platform where policy, industry, and cutting-edge research converge to build trust, resilience, and autonomy in advanced digital ecosystems. The conference is distinctly structured into three complementary pillars: a high-level Industry Day, where global technology leaders openly discuss real-world strategies and challenges in implementing digital sovereignty; practical training sessions that translate policy and innovation into actionable capabilities; and peer-reviewed research presentations, where leading researchers from top institutions present solutions across technological, legal, and societal dimensions of digital sovereignty. Building on the strong foundations of ICDS 2024 and the expanded international impact of ICDS 2025, the 3rd International Conference on Digital Sovereignty (ICDS 2026) will further strengthen Norway’s leadership at the forefront of global digital policy, innovation, and research, welcoming the international community to Oslo to shape the future of sovereign, secure, and sustainable digital infrastructure.  As in ICDS 2025, selected papers from the ICDS 2026 conference will be published in the Springer Proceedings on Complexity, further reinforcing the conference’s scientific quality and international visibility.Call for PapersWe have five tracks in ICDS 2026. Papers in any of these areas, especially with the following keywords covering and related to Digital Sovereignty, are welcome to be submitted.Track 1: Human-Centric Digital SovereigntyTrack 2: Industry and Innovation ImpactTrack 3: Digital Ecosystems and GovernanceTrack 4: National Digital Sovereignty and Societal ImpactTrack 5: Geopolitics and TrustPrevious EditionsICDS 2024 – publication: Elsevier Procedia Computer Science https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/procedia-computer-science/vol/254/suppl/CICDS 2025 – publication: Springer Proceedings in Complexity (SPCOM) https://link.springer.com/book/9783032215239Submission: https://easychair.org/my/conference?conf=icds20260The ICDS 2025 c onference is now in the process of soliciting submissions of original and innovative papers. Prospective authors are invited to submit papers in core and/or related areas of digital sovereignty. The detailed list of topics can be found in the ‘Call for Papers’. Each paper will be reviewed by three experts from the International Program Committee.Authors must submit an original full paper, 10 pages for Springer Proceedings on Complexity, that has not been previously published. All contributions must be written in English. Submissions will be evaluated based on relevance to conference themes (digital sovereignty, cybersecurity, data governance), originality and novelty, technical quality and rigor, clarity and organization, impact and significance, and, where applicable, ethical and responsible research practices, especially in areas such as AI and data use.Submission GuidelinesSubmissions to ICDS 2026 will follow a rigorous and transparent review process to ensure high-quality contributions. After the submission deadline, all papers will be screened by the editors for relevance and baseline quality. Suitable submissions will then be peer-reviewed by at least three independent experts. The editors will carefully evaluate the reviews and make recommendations based on consensus and merit. Finally, accepted papers will be reviewed by the chairs’ Steering Committee and Honorary Chair for final confirmation. Our goal is to maintain fairness, academic integrity, and constructive feedback throughout the process.Authors must submit an original full paper (6 -10 pages) that has not previously been published. All contributions must be written in English.Instructions for Authors of Springer Computer Science postings.conferenceName: Call for Book Reviews - Journal for Cultural and Religious Theory
postings.conferenceText: The editorial board of the Journal for Cultural and Religious Theory (JCRT), a Whitestone Publication, is pleased to announce the relaunch of its book review program. Effective immediately, JCRT is soliciting single-title reviews and cluster reviews from scholars working across religious studies, theology, philosophy of religion, critical theory, and adjacent fields.The relaunch responds directly to the void left by the closure of Reading Religion, the American Academy of Religion’s openly accessible book review site, which ceased active operations on May 31, 2026. With one of the largest open venues for scholarly religion reviews now transitioned to an archive, JCRT aims to help fill that gap by offering an open-access, peer-edited home for rigorous, timely, and theoretically engaged reviews.A call to a broad community of reviewersJCRT especially encourages graduate students and independent scholars to submit reviews, alongside tenure-track and established faculty. The editorial board views the relaunched review section as both a venue for serious critical engagement and an opportunity for emerging scholars to build publication records, sharpen their voices, and contribute to ongoing conversations in cultural and religious theory.“We want the review section to reflect the full range of scholars doing important work in our fields — from first-year doctoral students to senior colleagues,” said J.C. Smith, the book review editor. “Independent scholars and graduate students often produce the most incisive and generative reviews, and JCRT is committed to being a home for that work.”Submission formatsJCRT invites two primary formats:Individual book reviews — approximately 1,500 words, engaging a single recent title.Cluster reviews — approximately 2,000–2,500 words, engaging two to three thematically related titles in conversation.Reviews should combine substantive summary with critical, theoretically informed engagement consistent with JCRT’s longstanding editorial vision.How to submit or propose a reviewScholars interested in reviewing for JCRT — whether proposing a specific title, responding to a call, or offering to be added to the reviewer pool — should email the Book Review Editor at editor@jcrt.org with the subject line “JCRT-Review.” Please include a brief statement of interest, areas of expertise, and (if applicable) the title or titles you propose to review.Full submission guidelines are available at https://jcrt.org/submissions/About JCRTThe Journal for Cultural and Religious Theory is an open-access, peer-reviewed journal published by Whitestone Publications. Since its founding, JCRT has served as a leading venue for interdisciplinary work at the intersections of religion, theology, philosophy, and cultural theory, publishing scholars from around the world.ContactContact: JC Smith, Book Review Editor, editor@jcrt.orgWeb: https://jcrt.org###

postings.conferenceText: We invite submissions to the 1st Workshop on Decentralisation: Theory and Practice (DeTaP), to be held in association with Advances in Financial Technologies (AFT) 2026.Topics of interest include, but are not limited to:- Definitions and conceptualisations of decentralisation- Methods for measuring decentralisation- Critiques and limitations of existing measurement frameworks- Empirical studies of decentralisation in deployed systems- Decentralisation of blockchain governance- Legal tests for decentralisation and their relationship to technical definitions- Liability and accountability in decentralised systems- Optimal or “sufficient” degrees of decentralisation- Trade-offs between decentralisation and other system properties (e.g. efficiency, scalability, accountability)- Decentralisation of blockchain hardware and infrastructure- Case studies of endogenous and exogenous events shaping decentralisation- Causal analysis: drivers of decentralisation and centralisation pressures- Normative arguments for or against decentralisation- Decentralisation in other fields vs. blockchain-specific framing- Historical and non-blockchain case studies of decentralised systems, successful or unsuccessfulSubmissions require only a title and abstract describing the proposed talk. Authors may optionally submit a full or short paper alongside the abstract.The workshop has no proceedings and is intended as a venue for exchanging ideas, therefore work in progress and work that has been published at or submitted to another venue is equally welcome.Accepted papers may optionally be made available on the workshop's website at the authors' discretion.Submissions should be made via this form: https://forms.gle/3XGwZN2MbaG3vAZm6

postings.conferenceName: Special Session on Computational Methods for Intelligent Biofabrication: Models, Data and Reproducible Benchmarks - CompBioFab - Within BIOSTEC 2027
postings.conferenceText: Biofabrication, the automated generation of functional constructs from cells, biomaterials and bioactive molecules, still relies on trial-and-error design, and the cost of wet-lab iterations makes exhaustive experimentation infeasible. Intelligent Biofabrication replaces this with model-based, predictive engineering: simulators of cellular behaviour, hybrid multi-scale models and digital twins, protocol optimisation, and data-driven approaches learning from accumulated evidence.The CompBioFab Special Session, held within BIOSTEC 2027 in Valletta, Malta, is organised around interdisciplinary convergence, structured around shared benchmark problems, datasets and evaluation protocols. We invite submission of full papers and abstracts on the following topics of interest:- Multiscale Cellular Modeling: molecular to construct-scale formalisms, coupled- Biohybrid Robotics: living tissue fused with synthetic actuation- Computational & AI Biofabrication: machine learning for protocol design- Datasets & Reproducible Benchmarks: shared standards & evaluation protocols- Digital Twins & Bioreactors: simulated bioreactor processes & controls- Calibration & Uncertainty Quantification: validating models against experimental data- Organoids & In Vitro Models: New Approach Methodologies (NAMs)- Sustainable, Automated Workflows: resource-aware, reusable computational pipelinesPlease refer to the BIOSTEC 2027 submission guidelines for full paper/abstract formatting instructions.SUBMISSION LINK: https://biostec.scitevents.org/CompBioFabCO-CHAIRS Roberta Bardini, Politecnico di Torino, Italy Laurence Calzone, Institut Curie, France Miriam Filippi, ETH Zurich, Switzerland Diana Massai, Politecnico di Torino, ItalyCONTACT biostec.secretariat@insticc.org roberta.bardini@polito.it

postings.conferenceName: The 2nd International Workshop on Deep Learning for Biometrics and its Applications
postings.conferenceText: The 2nd International Workshop on Deep Learning for Biometrics and its Applications (DL4BA) will be held at Phoenix, Arizona, USA, in hybrid mode, from 14 to 17 december 2025, in conjunction with the IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData 2026, https://bigdataieee.org/BigData2026/).OverviewBiometrics has become a burgeoning research area due to the industrial and government needs for authentication, identification, security, and privacy concerns. Biometric technology has become useful solution for various applications including access control, surveillance and privacy, hardware security and forensics. During last decade, Deep Learning (DL) has received a great attention to solve difficult and complex problems in various domains. Its ability to automatically learn features from big data has made it a major asset.This workshop aims to present and discuss the recent advances on deep learning applied to biometrics providing innovative solutions to challenging problems in biometrics. It is an opportunity to bring researchers and experts together to discuss the current and future state of biometrics.Topics of interest include, but are not limited to, the following:- DL for biometrics-based authentication and identification- Deep biometric feature extraction- Deep biometric feature fusion- DL for biometric data analytics (signal, image, video, ...)- DL for biometric spoofing and deepfake detection- DL for big data challenges in biometrics- DL for multimodal biometrics- DL for soft biometrics- DL for forensic biometrics- DL for biometric security and privacy- Leveraging DL techniques for biometrics- Generative AI in biometrics- Federated learning in biometrics - Related applicationsImportant DatesOct. 1, 2026 (11:59 pm CST): Due date for full workshop papers submissionNov. 4, 2026: Notification of paper acceptance to authorsNov. 25, 2026: Camera-ready of accepted papersDec 14-17, 2026: WorkshopsPaper submissionPlease submit a full-length paper (up to 10 pages IEEE 2-column format including references) or a short-length paper (5 to 7 pages including references) through the online submission system (https://wi-lab.com/cyberchair/2026/bigdata26/index.php)Papers should be formatted to IEEE Computer Society Proceedings Manuscript Formatting Guidelines. postings.conferenceName: 5th International Workshop on Blockchain Security and Scalability (BSS 2026)
postings.conferenceText: CALL FOR PAPERS5th International Workshop on Blockchain Security and Scalability (BSS 2026)Co-located with IEEE Blockchain 202630 November–4 December 2026Université Marie et Louis Pasteur, Montbéliard, FranceWorkshop date: 30 November–4 December 2026 web: www.ibss.comABOUT THE WORKSHOPThe 5th International Workshop on Blockchain Security and Scalability (BSS 2026) invites researchers and practitioners from academia, industry and government to submit original research on the foundations, design, implementation and evaluation of blockchain and distributed ledger technologies.Blockchain systems support decentralised coordination across finance, healthcare, logistics, e-government, the Internet of Things, cyber-physical systems and next-generation networks. However, security weaknesses, privacy risks and scalability constraints continue to limit dependable real-world adoption.BSS 2026 provides a focused forum for research that addresses these challenges. The workshop welcomes theoretical work, system designs, empirical studies, reproducible evaluations, datasets, testbeds, case studies and critical analyses of deployed systems. Authors should state their threat models, assumptions, limitations and practical implications clearly.TOPICS OF INTERESTTopics include, but are not limited to:• Theories of blockchain and distributed ledger technology• New and modular blockchain architectures• Distributed consensus and fault-tolerance mechanisms• Blockchain security, privacy, trust and reputation• Attacks, vulnerabilities, fraud and forensic analysis• Scalability, performance optimisation, sharding and rollups• Cross-chain, bridge and off-chain technologies• Simulation, benchmarking and performance evaluation• Secure smart contracts, chain code, testing and verification• Authentication, authorisation and decentralised identity• Blockchain for artificial intelligence, IoT, cyber-physical systems, edge and cloud computing• Applications in healthcare, logistics, finance, e-government and Industry 4.0IMPORTANT DATESPaper submission:          20 September 2026Author notification:       15 October 2026Camera-ready submission:   22 October 2026Conference dates:          30 November–4 December 2026SUBMISSION LINKhttps://edas.info/newPaper.php?c=35179&track=139226PARTICIPATE AS A REVIEWERResearchers interested in joining the Programme Committee as reviewers should contact:muhammadajmal.azad@bcu.ac.ukWe look forward to receiving your submissions and welcoming you to BSS 2026 in Montbéliard, France.

postings.conferenceName: Knowledge and Natural Language Processing Track @ ACM SAC 2027
postings.conferenceText: Knowledge and Natural Language Processing Track @ ACM SAC 2027Aim and ScopeThe Knowledge and Natural Language Processing (KNLP) Track at the ACM Symposium on Applied Computing investigates methods and applications at the intersection of Knowledge Engineering and Natural Language Processing, with particular emphasis on approaches that combine these two areas.KNLP is an emerging and highly interdisciplinary research field at the core of Artificial Intelligence. It brings together and complements scientific advances in Natural Language Processing, Knowledge Representation and Reasoning, Machine Learning, and related disciplines.Topics of InterestTopics of interest include, but are not limited to, the following.Natural Language Processing    NLP methods for knowledge extraction    NLP for ontology population and ontology learning    Sentiment analysis and opinion mining for knowledge-based applications    Interplay between natural language and ontologies    NLP for explainable knowledge    Machine translation techniques for multilingual knowledge    NLP for the Web    Bias detection and mitigation in small and large language models    Interaction between small or large language models and knowledgeKnowledge    Knowledge-enhanced NLP    Knowledge for information retrieval    Knowledge-based sentiment analysis and opinion mining    Combining knowledge and deep learning for NLP    Knowledge technologies for the Web    Knowledge-enhanced agentic reasoning    Agent reasoning over knowledge graphs and ontologies    Knowledge-based agent personalization    Linked Data for NLP    Knowledge-based natural language explainability    Language-model-enhanced ontology and knowledge engineering methodologies and tools    Language-model-based agents for knowledge extraction, reasoning, and management    Ontology evaluation using small and large language models    Ontological knowledge representation and memorization in language models    Knowledge-based techniques for language models, including Retrieval-Augmented Generation, fact-checking, and bias mitigation    Question answering over knowledge graphs using small and large language modelsReal-World Applications Exploiting Knowledge and NLP    Knowledge and NLP systems for Big Data scenarios    Knowledge and NLP technologies supporting a diverse, equitable, and inclusive society    Deployment and evaluation of Knowledge and NLP systems in domains such as:        Digital Humanities and Social Sciences        eGovernment and public administration        Life sciences, healthcare, and medicine        News, media, and data-streaming environmentsPaper SubmissionWe invite original research papers and experience reports addressing the topics listed above.Submissions must not have been previously published or be under consideration for publication elsewhere. Papers must be submitted in PDF format using the official ACM SAC proceedings template.Authors’ names and affiliations must be entered separately in the submission system and must not appear in the submitted manuscript. All submissions will undergo a double-blind peer-review process in accordance with ACM SAC regulations.Submissions to the Student Research Competition (SRC) are also welcome. Prospective authors should consult the SAC 2027 SRC page for eligibility requirements and submission instructions.Submission Policy    All papers must initially be submitted as regular papers. There is no separate submission category for poster papers.    Papers will be evaluated according to their originality, technical contribution, presentation quality, and relevance to the Knowledge and Natural Language Processing Track.    Depending on the outcome of the review process and the overall acceptance-rate constraints, technically sound submissions that cannot be accepted as regular papers may be offered acceptance as posters.    Although there is no formal minimum page requirement, submissions shorter than four full pages that do not demonstrate a substantial contribution may be desk-rejected without external review.Submission Links    Regular papers and SRC abstracts: submission links are available through the ACM SAC 2027 website    Author kit and templates: formatting instructions and official templates are available through the ACM SAC 2027 websiteImportant DatesPlease consult the official ACM SAC 2027 website for up-to-date deadlines and possible changes.    October 2, 2026: Regular paper and SRC abstract submission    November 13, 2026: Author notification    November 28, 2026: Camera-ready copies of accepted papers and SRC submissions    December 5, 2026: Author registration deadline    April 5–9, 2027: Knowledge and Natural Language Processing Track at ACM SAC 2027All deadlines follow the time zone specified on the official conference website.Further InformationFor further information, please visit the Knowledge and Natural Language Processing Track website and the ACM SAC 2027 conference website.Questions may be addressed to the KNLP Track Co-Chairs.

postings.conferenceName: 1st Workshop on Virtual ISA for Rapidly Evolving Architectures @ MICRO 2026
postings.conferenceText: VISA 2026 examines the virtual ISA — a stable, hardware-agnostic abstraction between high-level programming models and diverse hardware backends — as the pivotal interface of the agentic era: the contract surface where LLM-driven code synthesizers, autonomous autotuners, compilers, and microarchitectural innovation meet. When the programmer is a machine, the ISA must be self-describing enough to reason over and verifiable enough to trust.The accelerator landscape is undergoing rapid and continuous transformation. However, this rapid architectural evolution introduces a critical fragmentation problem: each accelerator spawns its own toolchain, compiler backend, and software stack, leading to duplicated engineering effort, poor portability, and steep developer learning curves across targets. Virtual ISA enables compiler reuse across heterogeneous targets, rapid hardware prototyping, software longevity across architectural generations, and composable optimization at the right abstraction level.Despite this progress, the community lacks a dedicated venue for the cross-cutting challenges of Virtual ISA design, compilation, DSL integration, and co-design — the gap this workshop aims to fill.We invite short papers (4–6 pages, IEEE format) describing work in progress, position papers, vision papers, or early results. The scope spans the full accelerator stack — ISA design and semantics, compilation and optimization, DSLs and programming models, hardware co-design, and deployment experience.The agent-facing interface is the flagship theme that runs through all of them: wherever your work sits, we encourage you to ask how the problem changes when the primary reader and writer of the ISA is a machine.TOPICS OF INTERESTTopics include, but are not limited to:1. Agent-Facing Virtual ISA Interfaces- Self-describing virtual ISAs exposing semantics, costs, and resource footprints to LLM reasoners- Well-typed and verifiable contracts for reliable agent-generated code- Equivalence checking for machine-generated kernels- LLM-guided lowering and kernel synthesis- Closed-loop autotuning through the virtual ISA layer- Safety and sandboxing for agent-generated kernels- Benchmarks for the agent-programmability of virtual ISAs- Self-evolving virtual ISAs and lowering strategies2. Virtual ISA Design and Abstraction- Stable virtual ISA boundaries- Formal semantics and correctness- Versioning and compatibility strategies- Capability negotiation, feature discovery, and introspection- Effect systems, memory models, and concurrency semantics- Abstractions for heterogeneous architectures3. Virtual ISA and Architecture Co-design- Late binding of physical resources during virtual-to-physical lowering- Cost-model-aware virtual ISAs- Interfaces for parallelism, dataflow, precision, and locality- Reconfigurable and spatial architectures- Emerging hardware features and accelerator architectures- Dynamic-shape execution under stable semantics- Programmability–performance tradeoffs- AI acceleration, LLM serving, MoE, sparsity, processing-in-memory, chiplets, and KV-cache-oriented systems4. Compiler Optimizations- Lowering and legalization targeting virtual ISAs- Optimization across virtual and physical ISA boundaries- Polyhedral, tile-level, and search-based optimization- Profile-guided compilation- Equivalence checking and differential testing- LLM-aware compilation- Kernel fusion, scheduling, and graph partitioning- Directive- and annotation-guided compilation5. DSLs and Programming Models- Tile, dataflow, graph, and agentic pipeline languages- DSL frontends targeting virtual ISAs- Type systems for accelerator programming- Autotuning and search-based code generation- Programming abstractions for emerging AI workloads- LLM inference and training, MoE routing, long-context attention, KV-cache management, and multimodal or agentic serving- Profiling APIs and feedback-driven optimization6. Case Studies and Infrastructure- Virtual ISA deployments in AI, HPC, networking, and signal processing- Open-source frameworks and benchmarks- Simulation, modeling, and hardware/software co-design flows- Production experience with MLIR dialects, PTX, SPIR-V, StableHLO, TOSA, Triton-IR, CUDA Tile IR, Ascend PTO, and related systemsSUBMISSION GUIDELINESPaper length:4–6 pages using the IEEE conference two-column template.Paper types:Work-in-progress papers, position papers, vision papers, and early-results papers are welcome.Reviewing:The review process is single-blind. Author names and affiliations should appear in the submission.Submission site:https://visa2026.hotcrp.com/The HotCRP site is currently pending activation. Submissions will open after approval.Publication:Accepted papers will be presented at the workshop and posted on the VISA 2026 website. The workshop is non-archival, and submission does not preclude later publication at another venue.Presentation:At least one author of every accepted paper must register for the workshop through MICRO 2026 and present the work.Review process:Every submission will receive at least three reviews. Papers will be evaluated for relevance, originality, soundness, and potential to spark discussion.IMPORTANT DATESPaper submission deadline:September 25, 2026, 23:59 AoEAuthor notification:October 9, 2026, 23:59 AoECamera-ready papers:October 16, 2026, 23:59 AoEWorkshop:October 31, 202613:00–17:00 EETAthens, GreeceCONTACT AND FURTHER INFORMATIONWorkshop website:https://visaworkshop.github.io/2026/Call for Papers:https://visaworkshop.github.io/2026/cfp.htmlContact:visa.workshop.chairs@gmail.com

postings.conferenceName: Decolonising the Digital: Social Justice, Inclusion, and Equitable Knowledge Production
postings.conferenceText: Conference Theme+The DHARTI 2026 Biennial Conference seeks to foreground Digital Humanities as a critical site for interrogating questions of social justice, digital inclusion, digital justice, infrastructural access, representation, and epistemic inequality in and with the majority world.As digital and algorithmic technologies increasingly shape contemporary modes of knowledge production, pedagogy, archives, media circulation, and cultural participation, it becomes necessary to critically examine the uneven structures through which digitality operates. The conference aims to explore how Digital Humanities can move beyond techno-deterministic frameworks toward more inclusive, multilingual, community-oriented, and socially grounded practices.The conference welcomes scholars, researchers, educators, artists, archivists, technologists, activists, community practitioners, students, and engaged stakeholders across and beyond disciplines.Select papers will be published in a Scopus-Indexed Volume. The conference invites contributions on, but not limited to, the following areas, with a particular focus on Global Majority spaces and contexts:Decolonial tools and Decolonising Practices in Digital HumanitiesDigital Justice, Infrastructural Inequalities and Digital FuturesDigital Justice and Literary and Cultural ExpressionsCollaborative Knowledge Production and Digital SpaceArchives, Memory, and Digital PreservationLanguage Technologies and Multilingual FuturesDigital Pedagogy and Curricular PracticesVisual Cultures and Media EcologiesPlatform Studies and Algorithmic CulturesDigital Archives, Marginalized Communities, and Indigenous Knowledge SystemsDigital Humanities, Urban Studies, Mapping and SpatialityAccessibility and Inclusive Digital PracticesDigital Labour and Data PoliticsResponsible Computing, Data Ethics, and AI GovernanceParticipatory/Relational ML/AI practices/projects in India/Global SouthEthics, Surveillance, and Digital CitizenshipRace/ Class/ Caste/ Religion/ Gender and Digital HumanitiesBlack Digital Humanities and AfrofuturismDigital Humanities and Dalit FuturismEnvironmental Humanities and Digital EcologiesDigital Storytelling, Creative Practice, and Interactive MediaPublic Digital Humanities and Community EngagementModes of Participation+Modes of Participation:Academic Papers: 15-minute presentation followed by discussion.Panel Proposals: 3–4 papers around a common theme with a focus on ensuring plurality of representation and perspectives.In-person Poster Presentations: For emerging projects and research initiatives.Proposals for Workshops: The conference will be preceded by a set of pre-conference workshops. DHARTI members can propose workshops. Workshops will be scheduled on 18 Dec 2026 (Fri.).No participant shall serve as a lead presenter in more than one presentation. In the event that a presenter is shortlisted as a lead presenter for two or more papers after the review process, the Programme Committee will ask the participant to withdraw one of the papers. This rule shall not apply to workshops.Abstracts in Indian languages are encouraged. Posters may also be submitted in any Indian language. However, where an abstract or poster is submitted in an Indian language, an English version must also be provided to ensure that the content is accessible to the larger conference audience.All participants are required to be members of DHARTI (Digital Humanities Alliance for Research and Teaching Innovation). To encourage wider participation, undergraduate students may avail of a complimentary six-month membership, granted by DHARTI upon request. Those who wish to continue their membership beyond that period may register according to the prescribed membership criteria.Selected papers, following peer review and editorial evaluation, will be considered for publication in an edited conference proceedings volume.KIIT has secured a Letter of Intent from Peter Lang, an internationally reputed academic publisher, indicating its willingness to consider a select number of conference papers for publication. The proposed volume will subsequently be submitted for indexing in Scopus, subject to the publisher’s review and indexing requirements.

postings.conferenceName: 18th International Conference on Deontic Logic and Normative Systems, 29 June–1 July 2027, Hangzhou, China (First announcement)
postings.conferenceText: Dear colleagues,We are pleased to announce that DEON 2027, the 18th International Conference on Deontic Logic and Normative Systems, will be held at Zhejiang University in Hangzhou, China, from 29 June to 1 July 2027 — the first edition of the series to be held in Asia since its founding in 1991. The conference is hosted by the School of Philosophy of Zhejiang University and the Zhejiang University–University of Luxembourg Joint Lab on Advanced Intelligent Systems and Reasoning (ZLAIRE).The biennial DEON conference series brings together researchers interested in the formal study of normative concepts, normative reasoning, and normative systems, using methods from computer science, artificial intelligence, philosophy, linguistics, mathematics, and law. Topics include deontic logic, normative reasoning, legal reasoning, normative multi-agent systems, explainability, and trustworthy systems (full list on the website).The general theme of this edition is "Normativity under Uncertainty". Normative systems are inescapably confronted with uncertainty: agents must frequently deliberate about what ought to be done on the basis of information that is incomplete, imprecise, or conflicting — about the facts of the case, the norms in force, the consequences of action, or the reliability of one's sources. This edition investigates how central normative concepts, among them obligation, permission, responsibility, and blame, can be rigorously formalized, interpreted, and applied once the classical idealizations of certainty, consistency, and full information are lifted.Key dates (all Anywhere on Earth):Abstract submission deadline: 5 March 2027Paper submission deadline: 12 March 2027Notification of acceptance: 6 May 2027Conference: 29 June – 1 July 2027The conference will invite submissions of original and unpublished work (max. 15 pages, excluding references and technical appendix); reviewing will be double-blind. The proceedings will be published by College Publications as an open-access book. The full call for papers, including templates and the EasyChair submission link, will be released in November 2026.Programme committee co-chairs:Huimin Dong (TU Wien, Austria)Beishui Liao (Zhejiang University, China)Réka Markovich (University of Luxembourg, Luxembourg)Website: https://www.zlaire.net/deon2027/Contact: zhengzhoulogic@zju.edu.cnPlease save the date, and feel free to forward this announcement to interested colleagues and students.Best regards,The DEON 2027 Programme Committee Co-Chairs

postings.conferenceText: Conference on Cybersecurity and Applications (CCA’2026)25-26 November, 2026Sidi Abdallah, Algiers, ALGERIA.The National School of Cybersecurity (NSCS) and the Information System Security Agency (ASSI) are pleased to announce the organization of the 1st edition of the “Conference on Cybersecurity and Applications (CCA’2026)”, which will take place on November 25th–26th, 2026 at The “National School of Cybersecurity”, located within the “Scientific and Technological Hub Chahid “Abdelhafid Ihaddadene”, Sidi Abdallah, Algiers”.Currently, cybersecurity has become a cornerstone of trust, resilience, and sovereignty. With the rapid evolution of digital technologies, industrial and critical infrastructures, financial systems, healthcare services, and national security are increasingly exposed to cyber-attacks. Research in cybersecurity is therefore of paramount importance to develop new approaches, tools, and strategies for protecting data, systems, and users against malicious activities.The CCA’2026 conference will focus on shaping the future of cybersecurity in Algeria. The event will offer academics, researchers, engineers, professionals and policymakers the opportunity to interact and exchange ideas, and present recent advances of their research results, projects, investigative works, industrial experiences and innovations, and build collaborative solutions that address both current and future challenges in such a rapidly changing fields. It aims to bring together researchers, academics, practitioners, students and professionals to discuss recent advances, challenges, and applications in the field of cybersecurity. The CCA’2026 conference is organized into four main tracks. Academics, researchers, practitioners, students, and professionals are warmly invited to contribute and to submit their original research articles, surveys, technical reports, and case studies on, but not limited to, the following topics: # Track 1: Cryptography, Privacy, and Trusted Digital Systems o Cryptography and secure communications o Information-theoretic security in quantum systems o postings.conferenceText: ======================================================================CALL FOR PAPERS -- AID 20262nd IEEE PRDC Workshop on AI Dependability======================================================================Held in conjunction with the 31st IEEE Pacific Rim International Symposium on Dependable Computing (PRDC 2026).Where: Hong Kong SARWhen: one day within 2-4 December 2026 (the exact day will be announced on the workshop website)Website: https://aid2026-workshop.github.ioSubmit: https://easychair.org/conferences/?conf=aid2026))) PAPER SUBMISSION DEADLINE: 11 SEPTEMBER 2026 (AoE) (((======================================================================----------------------------------------------------------------------SCOPE----------------------------------------------------------------------The AID 2026 workshop provides a forum for researchers and industry practitioners to present and discuss the latest advancements in ensuring the dependability of AI and LLM-based systems. As AI becomes integral to critical infrastructure, its reliability, security, and robustness are paramount. This workshop will bring together experts from the dependable computing and AI communities to address new challenges in building trustable AI systems. We welcome submissions that explore innovative solutions, case studies, and fundamental research in this rapidly evolving field.----------------------------------------------------------------------TOPICS OF INTEREST----------------------------------------------------------------------Topics include but are not limited to:* AI-based Software Vulnerability Detection and Secure Code Generation* AI-based Attack Detection* LLM-based Rust Translation* AI-based Attack/Defense Simulation* AI-based Red Teaming* AI Model Attacks and Defenses* AI Dependability, Reliability, and Safety* Responsible and Trustworthy AI* Explainable AI (XAI)----------------------------------------------------------------------TWO SUBMISSION TRACKS----------------------------------------------------------------------* Regular Paper Track. Completed research, presented as a full conference paper with a clear contribution and supporting evaluation.* R&D Paper Track. Research carried out under a funded research project and still in progress. Papers introduce the project's objectives and approach and report interim findings, giving project teams a venue to present ongoing work and gather feedback.----------------------------------------------------------------------SUBMISSION GUIDELINES----------------------------------------------------------------------* Length. At most 6 pages, including figures, tables, and references.* Format. IEEE double-column conference template.* Review. Double-blind.* Originality. Original, unpublished, and not under review elsewhere.* Submission. Through EasyChair: https://easychair.org/conferences/?conf=aid2026----------------------------------------------------------------------PUBLICATION----------------------------------------------------------------------Accepted papers from both tracks will be published by the IEEE Computer Society Press (EI indexed) as part of the PRDC 2026 proceedings.----------------------------------------------------------------------IMPORTANT DATES (AoE)----------------------------------------------------------------------* Paper submission: 11 September 2026* Author notification: 9 October 2026* Camera ready submission: 20 October 2026----------------------------------------------------------------------COMMITTEES----------------------------------------------------------------------ORGANIZATION CHAIRS* Huy Kang Kim, Korea University* Dan Dongseong Kim, University of Queensland* Sangkyun Lee, Korea UniversityPROGRAM CHAIR* Hyunjae Kang, University of QueenslandPROGRAM COMMITTEE* Ah Reum Kang, Pai Chai University* Byung Il Kwak, Korea University* Hyoungshick Kim, Sungkyunkwan University* Hyun Min Song, Dankook University* Jeonghyun Lee, National Security Research Institute* Jiyoung Woo, Soonchunhyang University* Ke He, University of Canterbury* Ki-Woong Park, Sejong University* Mee Lan Han, Korea University* Mengmeng Ge, Monash University* Sang-Hoon Choi, Sejong University* Sanghoon Jeon, Kookmin University* Seonghoon Jeong, Sookmyung Women's University* Seungjin Ryu, National Security Research Institute* Taekyoung Kwon, Yonsei University======================================================================

postings.conferenceName: 34th International Colloquium On Structural Information and Communication Complexity
postings.conferenceText: =====================================SIROCCO 2027 Call for Papers=====================================34th International Colloquium On Structural Information and Communication ComplexityLarnaca, Cyprus, June 2–4, 2027, https://cyprusconferences.org/sirocco2027=====================================Important Dates=====================================Full paper submission: October 31, 2026 (AoE)Paper notification: January 30, 2027Conference dates: June 2–4, 2027=====================================About SIROCCO=====================================SIROCCO is devoted to the study of the interplay between structural knowledge, communication, and computing in decentralized systems that consist of multiple communicating entities. Special emphasis is given to innovative methodological and solution approaches that lead to a better understanding of the relationship between computing and communication.SIROCCO has a tradition of interesting and productive scientific meetings in a relaxed and pleasant atmosphere, attracting leading researchers in a variety of fields in which communication and knowledge play a significant role. Websites of past SIROCCO conferences can be found at https://sirocco.hiit.fi. The proceedings of past SIROCCO conferences can be found at https://link.springer.com/conference/sirocco.=====================================Scope=====================================Original papers are solicited from all areas of study of local structural knowledge and global communication and computational complexities.Typical but not exclusive topics of interest include the following (in alphabetical order).•	Biological and nature-inspired distributed algorithms•	Blockchains and related distributed paradigms•	Distributed algorithms and computability•	Distributed graph algorithms•	Distributed quantum computing•	Epistemic modeling and analysis of distributed systems•	Fault tolerance•	Formal verification of distributed systems•	Game theory in distributed computing•	Mobile agents and autonomous distributed systems•	Network modeling and analysis•	Security in distributed computing•	Self-stabilization•	Shared-memory algorithms•	Structural and communication complexity analysis•	Topology in distributed computing•	Wireless, ad-hoc, and peer-to-peer networksKeeping with the tradition of SIROCCO, submissions on new areas related to the general scope of the conference are also welcome.=====================================Submission Instructions=====================================Submissions must report on original research and contain results that have not appeared previously in a regular conference paper and that have not been concurrently submitted to or previously published in a journal or a conference with published proceedings.Submission format. Manuscripts must be submitted in PDF format using EasyChair. Submissions must be written in English and formatted in a single-column format on US letter-size or A4 paper, use at least 11-point font, and have at least 2.5 cm margins.Submission length. All submissions must start with a cover page, which will include the paper’s title, a short abstract, and, preferably, keywords.There is no page limit, and authors are encouraged to submit the full version of their paper. The submission should contain, within the first 12 pages (excluding the cover page and bibliographic references), a concise and clear presentation of the primary content and merits of the work.Content beyond the cover page, references, and the first 12 pages will be read at the discretion of the reviewers only.A submission that is not accepted as a full paper may be invited as a brief announcement.Double-blind reviewing. SIROCCO 2027 will employ a lightweight double-blind reviewing process. Submissions should not reveal the identity of the authors in any way (e.g., author names, affiliations, email addresses, and funding information should not appear in the submission). However, authors are free to disseminate draft versions of their submissions as they normally would (e.g., by posting drafts on the web). Questions about the double-blind reviewing process may be directed to the PC chair by email.Submission website. Paper submissions will be handled by EasyChair, so please make sure that you have an active account. Papers must be submitted electronically at https://easychair.org/conferences/?conf=sirocco2027.Submissions deviating from these guidelines as well as papers outside the general scope of the conference may be rejected without consideration of their merits.=====================================AI policy=====================================AI policy for authors.  All authors of a submission must be human and are fully responsible for the integrity, originality, and copyright of their submission.Authors may use AI tools for limited purposes such as language editing (e.g., fixing typos or improving grammar) without the need for disclosure.Any other use of AI tools (including LLMs) must be clearly disclosed in the submission in an AI-disclosure section, and authors must specify which tool was used and for what purpose.Any undisclosed use of AI tools, or inaccurate representation of AI-generated or AI-modified content, may lead to rejection of the submission or further action.AI policy for reviewers.  Reviewers may use LLM-based tools to assist with the review process, provided that the confidentiality of the content of the submissions is preserved. However, the review itself must be written solely by the reviewer and must not be drafted, generated, or rewritten with the assistance of AI tools.Reviewers must rely on their own judgment and retain full responsibility for the content and conclusions of their reviews.=====================================Proceedings=====================================The proceedings of SIROCCO 2027 will be published by Springer in the Lecture Notes in Computer Science (LNCS) series. Please note that inclusion in the proceedings requires an in-person presentation by one of the authors at the conference and at least one full registration for each paper.=====================================Best Paper Awards=====================================All regular papers are eligible for the best paper award. Moreover, all regular papers with at least one student author, where the student author(s) have contributed most of the work, are also eligible for the best student paper award. If a submission is eligible for the best student paper award, please state this on the cover page.The Program Committee may choose not to make the awards or to split them among multiple papers.=====================================Special Issue=====================================Selected papers from SIROCCO 2027 will be invited to a special issue of the journal Theoretical Computer Science.=====================================Program Committee=====================================Emmanuelle Anceaume - CNRS, IRISA, Université de RennesJames Aspnes - Yale UniversityHagit Attiya - TechnionAlkida Balliu - Gran Sasso Science Institute (Chair)Petra Berenbrink - University of HamburgQuentin Bramas - University of StrasbourgYi-Jun Chang - National University of SingaporeArtur Czumaj - University of WarwickFrancesco d'Amore - Gran Sasso Science InstitutePeter Davies-Peck - Durham UniversityMichael Elkin - Ben-Gurion University of the NegevLaurent Feuilloley - CNRS, LIRIS, Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1Orr Fischer - University of HaifaMaxime Flin - Aalto UniversityPierre Fraigniaud - CNRS, IRIF, Université Paris CitéDiana Ghinea - Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and ArtsGeorge Giakkoupis - Inria, Université de RennesMagnús M. postings.conferenceName: TIDEL Scholarly Symposium Faith, Ethics, and Digital Transformation
postings.conferenceText: # TIDEL Scholarly Symposium Faith, Ethics, and Digital TransformationJoin TIDEL for a two-day convening exploring the ethical, theological, social, and institutional implications of technological change in an era of rapid innovation and profound social transformation.Founded in 2022, TIDEL is a Union Theological Seminary–based initiative that brings together faith leaders, scholars, technologists, nonprofit practitioners, and public leaders to explore ethical, justice-centered, and collaborative approaches to technology, innovation, and digital engagement.***## OverviewThursday, October 1, 2026Union Theological Seminary1:45 PM -- 5:45 PMBoxed lunch available at 12:45 PM$100 until September 1$150 afterYou do NOT have to register to submit a paper. All paper submissions are at no cost. 3 papers will be selected per theme. If your paper is selected, your registration fee will be waived.Registration for the symposium is open to all. You DO NOT have to submit a paper in order to attend the symposium.Sessions, panel discussions, and interdisciplinary dialogue among scholars, practitioners, technologists, faith leaders, and graduate students exploring critical questions at the intersection of technology, theology, ethics, innovation, and public life.### Call for Papers Themes### Reimagining Human Flourishing in the Digital AgeDisruptive inquiry into how AI, automation, and digital ecosystems reshape identity, belonging, meaning-making, and spiritual life --- and what it means to thrive when the boundaries between human and machine blur.### Racial Justice in the Digital Public SquareUnapologetic interrogation of how technology amplifies or dismantles systems of racial power. Examining algorithmic bias, platform monopolies, digital redlining, and the urgent fight for an equitable, democratic digital public square.### The Futuring of Faith Communities: Digital Religion, Leadership, and BelongingForward-looking inquiry into how digital culture, online ritual, hybrid community, and emerging tools are reshaping religious leadership, congregational life, and the meaning of belonging — and how faith communities can cultivate resilient, imaginative futures.### Details- **Deadline to submit papers: September 15.**- **Notifications by September 22.**[Submit a Paper](https://www.tidelconference.org/submit-paper)

postings.conferenceName: WORKSHOP ON INTERNET OF THINGS IN HEALTH RESEARCH
postings.conferenceText: 5TH IOT-HR: WORKSHOP ON INTERNET OF THINGS IN HEALTH RESEARCHCo-located with IEEE Annual Congress on Artificial Intelligence of Things (IEEE AIoT)Aim and Scope:The IoT-HR Workshop explores the challenges and opportunities of continuous data acquisition from Internet of Things (IoT) devices, such as smartwatches, fitness trackers, mobile phones, and ambient sensors, for medical research and digital health. While these systems offer rich insights into daily living and physical well-being, critical hurdles remain in integration, data quality, data processing, user adoption, privacy, and clinical validity.The workshop provides a collaborative venue bringing together academic researchers, industry experts, and practitioners to address these core challenges. By identifying innovative strategies and optimizing IoT data usage in health, IoT-HR contributes directly to IEEE AIoT 2026 by expanding its scope into high-impact healthcare and digital well-being applications.Topics:We invite submissions addressing, but not limited to, the following:● Use of IoT systems for health research● IoT and electronic Patient-Reported Outcomes (ePRO) / electronic Clinical Outcome Assessment (eCOA)● IoT-based telehealth and home monitoring systems● IoT-based Active and Healthy Ageing technologies● Hardware/software platforms for health research● Algorithms and methods for gathering clinically relevant knowledge from IoT devices● Security, privacy, and trust in IoT for health applications● Clinical trials and pilot studies involving IoTFormat:We welcome full research papers, work-in-progress submissions, and demonstration abstracts. All submissions will be peer-reviewed by at least three TPC members. Accepted papers will be presented at the workshop.Paper submission:Manuscript templates can be found athttps://www.ieee.org/conferences/publishing/templates.htmlAll submissions to IoT-HR must be uploaded to EasyChair at https://easychair.org/conferences/?conf=ieeeaiot2026.Publication:All accepted and presented papers will be submitted to IEEE Xplore.Workshop Chairs:- Filippo Palumbo, CNR, Italy- Dario Salvi, Malmo University, Sweden- Alessandra Angelucci, Politecnico di Milano, ItalyImportant Dates:Paper Submission deadline: 30th September 2026 HARD DEADLINENotification deadline: 7nth October 2026Camera-ready deadline: 21st October 2026

postings.conferenceName: 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Cyber Physical Systems
postings.conferenceText: The International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Cyber Physical Systems (CICPS 2027) aims to provide a dynamic and interdisciplinary platform to explore the convergence of Computational Intelligence (CI) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS)—a fusion that is transforming the way we design, operate, and secure the intelligent systems of tomorrow.Computational Intelligence techniques—rooted in nature-inspired, adaptive, and learning-based algorithms—offer innovative solutions for complex, uncertain, and nonlinear real-world problems. On the other hand, Cyber-Physical Systems represent a new generation of engineered systems that tightly integrate computation, networking, and physical processes, often interacting with human supervisors.Together, these disciplines are driving technological breakthroughs across sectors such as autonomous systems, agriculture, aerospace, infrastructure, energy, environmental monitoring, healthcare, manufacturing, and transportation. CICPS 2027 will convene top researchers, practitioners, and industry leaders to showcase state-of-the-art innovations and chart a course for future developments that promise profound societal and economic impact.
